page.layout: One printed page, number 609 at the head. One column of running text. Below it a centred block of six lines in Syriac script. Then running text continues to the foot. Catchword and signature at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Maria Virgo Sancta, Mater Iesu Saluatoris nostri, supplica, & deprecare misericordias peccatoribus, ne pereant. Qui ad tuas orationes confugiunt, oratio tua sit illis murus in hoc Mundo, atque in futuro. Ibidem ad Sanctos:

Beati sunt iusti, qui dilexerunt te, Seruator noster, & mandata custodierunt tua, ac voluntatem perfecerunt. Virtus abdita in ipsis custodiat Mundum, sintque in Ecclesia scaturigines auxiliorum. Infirmi sanentur, & curentur, claudi ambulent, & erigantur ab auxiliis officium ipsorum.

Quid plura? omnia sane Orientalium, quos pro se laudat Hottingerus, sine ulla tamen probatione, symbolica scripta huiusmodi formulis refertissima[?] sunt. Quamobrem unam producamus nunc, vel alteram formulam ex ijs, quibus Romana vti-tur Ecclesia, ut collatione facta cum mox allatis, videant aequi, & probi Lectores,

page.notes: The six Syriac lines are printed in Syriac script and are not legible to me at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible rather than guessed. The first line of the Latin after the Syriac, "Beati sunt iusti", is a Latin translation and was read clearly. Long s was rendered as plain s in "symbolica", "scripta", "scaturigines" and "sanentur". The word "refertissima" is doubtful because the long s and double letters are blurred. The right and left edges of the page show ink bleed-through from the reverse side, which was not transcribed. Some words are slightly smudged but readable.
